ActiveMatchResponse.description: The match a player is playing, for a proxy offering them a rejoin.

gameServerName.description: The GameServer, as the proxy has it registered.

AssignmentResponse.description: The server a matched player should be routed to.

gameServerName.description: The Agones GameServer name, which is also the Velocity backend name.

address.description: Fallback route. The routing pipeline resolves the name; the raw endpoint ships alongside it for the case where it has not.

BandRequestBody.description: band(t) = max(b0, k*sigma) + w*floor(waitSeconds/sSeconds). Any field that is absent, null or not positive falls back to its default — the same rule the gRPC surface applies to a zero, so a caller porting its code keeps the behaviour it had.

mercySeconds.description: After this wait the anchor's band goes unbounded — the whole ladder.

mutualSeconds.description: After this wait the anchor stops requiring mutual band overlap.

BoardBody.description: A stat board a mode writes.

displayName.description: Max 64 characters. Omit to show the stat.

cancelled.description: False when the ticket is past withdrawing — its match is being allocated or its players have been sent — or is not this player's. A legitimate answer, not an error. A ticket whose match's server is still preparing the round (PREPARING) can be withdrawn.

EnqueueRequestBody.description: Ask for a match in a mode.

playerId.description: Player UUID — the Keycloak identity, stable across sessions.

map.description: The map to play, `<namespace>/<name>`, from the mode's pool (GET /v1/match/modes/{modeId}/maps). Omit for any map. The player is then only matched with players who asked for the same map or for none. 400 if the map is not in the pool, or the mode has no maps.

EnqueueResponse.description: The ticket a player now holds.

mu.description: The player's current mu for this mode, so a client can show a rating without a second round trip.

queuePosition.description: How many tickets are queued for the mode, this one included.

MapsBody.description: Where a mode's maps come from and how one is chosen.

namespace.description: Every map pinned for this environment under `<namespace>/` is in the pool. A namespace may itself contain a slash.

selection.description: How a match's map is chosen when none of its players asked for one. RANDOM (default): uniformly from the pool, preferring maps that ship a pre-lit world.

MatchPresenceRequestBody.description: Whether the player is in their match right now.

connected.description: False when the player dropped off the network: the match is kept for the rejoin grace only. True once they are back in it.

MatchReadyRequestBody.description: Whether the round a server was preparing for a match is ready.

gameServerName.description: The reporting server's GameServer name; must be the match's server.

ok.description: True when the round is ready for its players, false when it could not be.

reason.description: Why not, for operators. Never interpreted.

MatchReadyResponse.description: Whether the match's players are being sent to the server.

routed.description: True: the players are routed (also on a retry after that). False: the match is no longer waiting for this server — it timed out, failed, too many players left, or the server reported it could not prepare — and the server should discard the round.

ModeMapsResponse.description: The maps a mode can be queued for.

maps.description: Pinned map addresses, sorted. Empty for a mode without maps.

selection.description: How a map is chosen when a ticket asks for none; null without maps.

ModeResponse.description: A live mode, as the lobby lists it.

displayName.description: The mode id when the mode registered none.

leases.description: Unexpired leases. Zero for a permanent mode.

permanent.description: True for a mode never registered with a lease.

ModesResponse.description: Every live mode: permanent, or leased with at least one live lease.

placement.description: 1-based finishing position, lower is better. Ties repeat a placement. Weng-Lin needs a ranking rather than a win/loss bit: without one a multi-team result degrades to winner-versus-rest, which biases the ladder.

QueueStatsResponse.description: Queue depth for a mode, for UI.

available.description: False when the mode has no matchmaking config — nobody can queue.

RatingResponse.description: A player's Weng-Lin rating for one mode. Ratings are global, not per region.

results.description: One entry per player. At least one.

terminationReason.description: Stored for operators, never interpreted. Defaults to `normal_finish`.

applied.description: False when this result had already been recorded — the call was a retry, not an error.

rated.description: True when the match was ranked and ratings actually moved.

queued.description: True when the result was accepted onto the result stream and the ladder moves asynchronously, within seconds. `applied` and `rated` then say what will happen. False when it was applied before this answer.

state.description: QUEUED, MATCHED, PREPARING, ASSIGNED, CANCELLED or FAILED. PREPARING: the match has a server that is preparing the round; the player is not routed until it is ASSIGNED. A caller that does not know a state treats it as still waiting.

assignment.description: Set exactly when state is ASSIGNED.

UpsertQueueRequestBody.description: A mode's matchmaking configuration, as forge pushes it from the `matchmaking:` block in grounds.yaml. There is no hot reload: the next queue tick picks it up.

teamCount.description: Teams per match. At least 2 — a match needs an opponent.

ranked.description: Whether results move ratings. Decided here, at configuration time, and never by the result call — that is what stops an ephemeral test workspace polluting the ladder.

band.description: Banding parameters. Omit for the defaults.

fleetName.description: The Agones Fleet that serves this mode. Omit when the fleet is named after the mode, which is the usual case. Set it when one image serves several modes — a duel server builds a different arena per mode and runs all of them from one pool, and a fleet per mode would idle a set of servers for each.

minPlayers.description: The fewest players a match may start with. Omit for teamSize * teamCount, which always waits for a full match. Lower only for a free-for-all (teamSize 1): after fillSeconds an under-filled match forms from whoever is queued, as long as that is at least this many.

fillSeconds.description: How long the longest-waiting player waits for a full match before an under-filled one forms. Ignored unless minPlayers is lowered.

leaseId.description: Identity of the registering game server, its HOSTNAME. Present makes this registration a lease: the mode then exists only while at least one lease is unexpired. Omit for a permanent mode.

leaseSeconds.description: Lease TTL in seconds, 15..600. Renewed by repeating the PUT. Default 60.

displayName.description: Shown in the lobby. Max 64 characters. Omit to show the mode id.

icon.description: Minecraft item key for the lobby, e.g. `minecraft:iron_sword`.

boards.description: Stat boards the game writes as `<modeId>.<stat>`. The first is the default for /leaderboard.

rejoinEnabled.description: Whether a disconnected player may rejoin a running match.

maps.description: The mode's map pool. Omit for a mode without maps: its matches are pushed with no map, and a ticket cannot ask for one.

UpsertQueueResponse.description: Whether the upsert created the mode or replaced an existing config.

bearerAuth.description: Projected ServiceAccount token with the grounds-services audience.

info.description:
The matchmaker: players queue per mode, the service forms MMR-based matches, allocates an Agones GameServer and hands the proxy somewhere to route them. Results reported here are what move the Weng-Lin ladder.

There is no project or region anywhere in this API. service-match runs inside the project's own vCluster, which is the tenancy boundary — a caller cannot address another project because it cannot reach another project's matchmaker.

post.description: `ok: true` on a match that is PREPARING on this server routes its players (`routed: true`; a retry once routed answers the same). `ok: false` puts them back on the queue with the wait they had earned. A match that is no longer waiting for this server — timed out, failed, left by too many players, or unknown — answers `routed: false`, and the server should discard the round.

post.summary: Queue a player for a mode
post.description:
Rejected with 409 if the player already holds a live ticket — one live ticket per player, worldwide, is what stops a player being committed to two matches.

There is deliberately no project or region in the body. service-match runs inside the project's own vCluster, so the vCluster is the tenancy boundary: a ticket cannot address another project because it cannot reach another project's matchmaker. Accepting either field here would hand that boundary to the caller.

400.description: playerId or modeId is missing or not a UUID, or the requested map is not in the mode's pool (or the mode has no maps).

404.description: The mode has no matchmaking config.

409.description: The player already holds a live ticket.

get.description: The source of truth on reconnect, and the only authority on an assignment: the NATS assignment push is a wakeup, this is the answer.

200.description: The ticket's state, and its assignment once it has one.

delete.description: Succeeds while the ticket is QUEUED, and while it is PREPARING — its match's server is still preparing the round. A preparing match left with fewer than the mode's minPlayers fails and its other players go back on the queue; otherwise it goes ahead without this one. Once a match is being allocated (MATCHED) or its players are sent (ASSIGNED) the ticket is committed: `cancelled: false` is the answer for that case and for a ticket that is not this player's; neither is an error.

400.description: ticketId or playerId is missing or malformed.
